plans.objective: [DIM: NEW] The solution space rigidity is determined by the algebraic structure of the constraint equations: linear constraints produce a rigid (unique) solution space while nonlinear constraints produce a fat (continuous) solution space, detectable via the network capacity trend N_c(w). | pro: Purely mathematical, adheres to all constraints, and directly tests the core hypothesis through a controlled construction. con: Requires careful design of constraint equations to ensure the expected behavior.

steps.description: Implement the numerical experiment to test the hypothesis that solution space rigidity is determined by the algebraic structure of constraint equations. Create a Python script that: (1) constructs linear (rigid) and nonlinear (fat) constraint families, (2) trains small feedforward networks using scipy.optimize.minimize with L-BFGS-B to find minimum network capacity N_c(w) achieving zero violation (validation error ≤ 1e-3), (3) performs multi-seed optimization to avoid local minima, and (4) outputs the N_c(w) trend analysis. The script must include the zero-violation reachability anchor (step 0) and report all required metrics.
